requirement: Dispatch planning and execution are connected through the public dispatch entry.
finding: The public dispatch entry src/dispatch/index.mjs re-exports only normalize, queue, capacity, access, schedule, retry, serialize, storage, manifest, publisher and telemetry (lines 1-11). It has no re-export of executor.mjs, so the execution operations defined there (executeAuthorizedPlan, executeDryRun, runEligibleStops, emitPlanCreated, pendingStops) are not reachable through the public entry, while planning operations such as createDispatchPlan, savePlan and previewPlan are.

requirement: Under dispatch-policy, nextRetryDelay applies the Retry timing rules to every server-provided retryAfter.
finding: nextRetryDelay (src/dispatch/retry.mjs:24) takes the retry-after path only when retryAfter is truthy. A server-provided retryAfter of 0 is a finite numeric value that must replace the computed backoff under rule 7 (dispatch-policy.md:16), but it falls through to computeBackoff. Infinity is truthy, so it reaches retryAfterDelay and yields the 2000 ms cap, although rule 7 applies only to finite numeric values.

requirement: executeAuthorizedPlan rejects an unauthorized caller before invoking dispatch.
finding: Line 4 evaluates await dispatchRoute(dispatch, route) as an argument before unlessForbidden (line 6) applies the canPlanRoute result. The dispatch function is therefore invoked even when the caller is unauthorized, and the authorization result is applied only to the outcome afterwards.

requirement: Under dispatch-policy, stopsForDriver returns exactly the stops whose assigned driver is the given driver.
finding: stopsForDriver (queue.mjs:30) compares only stop.driver. Under rule 30 (dispatch-policy.md:63) the assigned driver of a reassigned stop is the driver of its reassignment, which driverWorkload (capacity.mjs:18) handles. A stop reassigned to the given driver is therefore omitted, and a stop whose original driver matches but whose reassignment names another driver is wrongly included.

requirement: Under storage-contract, writePlanAtomically renames the temporary bytes only after they are durable.
Under dispatch-policy, chooseDeparture applies every Departure timing rule.
finding: Rule 14 (dispatch-policy.md:26) is not applied. A departure at 03:xx UTC is inside the 2-4 departure window (schedule.mjs:1) and inside the 3-5 blackout, so line 6 moves it with atUtcHour(date, 5) to 05:00 UTC. 05:00 is outside the window, but chooseDeparture returns it instead of refusing it, and no window check follows the blackout move.

requirement: redactNestedDriverToken removes a nested driver token from telemetry.
emitPlanCreated emits plan.created only after storage succeeds.
finding: emitPlanCreated (executor.mjs:14-17) passes onStored as the onCommit option of store.write (storage.mjs:4). The Plan Store Contract (storage-contract.md:9-15) does not define store.write, so the governing documents do not establish whether onCommit runs only after the plan is durably stored. The emission timing is unverified rather than contradicted.

requirement: Under dispatch-policy, hasDuplicateRouteKeys reports duplicates exactly when two stops are duplicates.
finding: Line 18 builds each identity by concatenating depotId and normalized routeKey with no separator. Rule 19 (dispatch-policy.md:37) defines the identity as the pair of depotId and normalizeRouteKey(routeKey). Stops with depotId 'A' and routeKey '1B' and stops with depotId 'A1' and routeKey 'B' both produce 'A1B', so distinct identities are reported as duplicates.

requirement: Under dispatch-policy, parseRetryCount accepts exactly the valid retry counts and otherwise returns a result whose ok is false.
finding: Line 4 treats a value as valid when Number(value) is an integer from 0 through 3. Rule 22 (dispatch-policy.md:43) makes text valid only when it is one or more base-10 digits, and rule 21 (line 42) limits valid counts to whole numbers. Values such as an empty string (Number('') is 0), ' 2 ', '0x2', '1e0', null and false are accepted with ok true, so the function does not reject every other value.

requirement: remainingVehicleCapacity never returns a negative value.
Under dispatch-policy, pendingStops returns every stop except the delivered stops.
finding: Line 19 excludes only stops whose state is delivered. Rule 31 (dispatch-policy.md:64) defines a delivered stop as one whose state is delivered or handedOver, so handedOver stops are wrongly returned as pending.

requirement: previewPlan returns a dry-run result without invoking storage.
redactAccessLog removes token and secret fields while preserving other fields.
orderedDestinationGroups returns the destination groups of the records in ascending lexical order.
finding: orderedDestinationGroups passes the Map returned by groupByDestination to orderManifestGroups. Line 11 spreads the Map into [key, group] entry arrays and compares their destination property, which is undefined for those arrays. The comparator therefore always returns 0, and the groups keep Map insertion order instead of ascending lexical order.

requirement: routeDistance rejects when no road connects two consecutive points.
savePlan validates a plan before the first persistent write.
computeBackoff doubles from 250 milliseconds and caps the result at 2000 milliseconds.
retryTransient permits retries only for errors explicitly marked transient.
Under adapter-contracts, locateStops leaves out every stop whose address the geocoder does not know.
finding: geocoder.lookup is specified only for known addresses (adapter-contracts.md:3). It does not state the result for an unknown address. locateStops (queue.mjs:34) keeps stops whose lookup result is not undefined, which assumes an unknown address resolves to undefined. The contract does not establish that, so the requirement cannot be decided from the governing documents.

requirement: retainScheduleOffset preserves the supplied offset exactly.
runEligibleStops skips cancelled stops while retaining the other stop order.
Under dispatch-policy, withinVehicleCapacity accepts a total equal to the configured limit.
finding: withinVehicleCapacity (capacity.mjs:3) converts the kilogram limit to grams (limit * 1000) and accepts only when remainingVehicleCapacity(...) > 0. When the total equals the limit, the remaining capacity is 0 and the total is rejected. Canonical unit handling in rules 28-29 (dispatch-policy.md:58-59) is not the cause; the strict comparison excludes equality.

requirement: Under dispatch-policy, canPlanRoute treats an actor holding routes:admin as owning every depot.
finding: Line 3 checks actor.scopes for routes:admin, which omits scopes granted by active claims. Rule 3 (dispatch-policy.md:9) applies to held scopes, and rule 4 (line 10) defines held scopes as own scopes plus active claim scopes. An actor whose routes:admin comes from an active claim is not treated as owning every depot, while effectiveScopes (line 5) does include claim scopes for the routes:plan check.

requirement: Under dispatch-policy, canPlanRoute refuses every suspended actor.
finding: effectiveScopes (line 5) drops actor.scopes for a suspended actor but keeps every active claim scope. A suspended actor with an active claim granting routes:plan passes the first check on line 3, and when its depotId matches the route (requireDepotOwner, line 14), canPlanRoute returns true. Rule 5 (dispatch-policy.md:11) says a suspended actor has no held scopes.

requirement: selectActiveClaims excludes claims before their start and at or after expiry.
checksumPlan hashes the bytes returned by the plan serializer.
Dispatch manifest publication is connected through the public dispatch entry.
safeAnnouncement omits a top-level credential from the announcement payload.
encodeUtf8 encodes publication bytes as UTF-8.
manifestEntryIsValid rejects blank package IDs.
Under storage-contract, publishWithAnnouncement removes the stored manifest when announcement delivery fails.
finding: handleAnnouncementFailure (manifest.mjs:32) calls store.remove on the value returned by store.get. Per storage-contract.md:6, store.get resolves to a new copy of the stored manifest. Per line 7, store.remove removes a stored manifest only when given that exact stored object and removes nothing for any other value. The manifest written at publisher.mjs:11 therefore remains stored after an announcement failure.

requirement: Under dispatch-policy, redactManifestEvent removes every credential nested below an auth field.
finding: stripCredentials (telemetry.mjs:14) recurses only into values whose constructor is Object. Arrays are returned unchanged, so a credential inside an array under auth (for example auth.sessions[0].token) is kept. Rule 24 (dispatch-policy.md:48) requires removal at every depth of the redacted value.

requirement: Given a positive integer maximum, chunkManifest limits every non-empty chunk to that configured maximum.
Under storage-contract, publishWithAnnouncement waits for the exact manifest to be durably stored before sending its announcement.
serializeManifestRecords emits NDJSON with one LF after every record, including the last.
orderManifestGroups orders destination groups in ascending lexical order.
Under dispatch-policy, manifestRecipients lists the contact phone of every manifest entry that has a phone.
publicationResult returns structured success and failure variants.
normalizedPlanKey trims and uppercases the route-key storage segment.
buildManifest copies record objects instead of mutating supplied records.
finding: buildManifest copies each record with a spread (line 26), but labelDriver (line 34) calls Object.assign on the supplied driver object, which changes the label inside the caller's record and in the copy. For a driver object without a label, preserveManifestDriver(undefined) yields the string 'undefined', and that string is written into the driver.

requirement: Under dispatch-policy, publishWithRetry stops after the allowed number of publication attempts.
publishManifest stores the manifest only when every entry is valid.
finding: Line 5 maps entries through an async function, so checks is an array of Promise objects. Promise objects are truthy, so checks.every(Boolean) on line 6 is always true. An invalid entry therefore does not return invalid-manifest, and stageManifest (line 7) stores the manifest.

requirement: successTelemetry records the success event, manifest ID, and timestamp.
groupByDestination groups records using normalized destination keys.
Under dispatch-policy, departureMinute is a stop's arrivalMinute plus its service time.
Under dispatch-policy, publishWithRetry retries only failures that the Failure classification rules make transient.
finding: asPublicationError (publisher.mjs:19) sets transient to true whenever retryAfter is finite, even when the failure is marked transient: false. Rule 27 (dispatch-policy.md:54) is later than rule 26 (line 53) in the same Failure classification section and therefore overrides it: a failure marked transient: false is never transient. publishWithRetry still retries such a failure.

requirement: preserveManifestDriver trims driver labels without changing letter case.
coalescePackages removes duplicate package IDs across the complete manifest.
finding: coalesceAcrossGroups tests normalized IDs against seen (line 37), but adds the raw group.packageIds to seen (line 38). An ID kept in raw form such as ' P1 ' is therefore not recognized when the same ID appears as 'P1' in a later group, and that duplicate remains in the manifest.

requirement: Stop ordering uses descending priority followed by ascending sequence.
Publication audit records include action, actor, and timestamp.
Window membership includes both the declared start and end hour.
Schedule offsets pass through without coercion.
Under dispatch-policy, a route duration adds the travel minutes and the service time of every stop.
finding: routeDuration (queue.mjs:32) adds serviceMinutes but not the 5 parking minutes that rule 32 (dispatch-policy.md:65) includes in a stop's service time. Each stop's contribution is understated by 5 minutes.

requirement: Under dispatch-policy, manifest-event redaction removes every credential nested inside authentication data.
finding: Same root cause as the issue 02 manifest-event redaction finding: stripCredentials (telemetry.mjs:14) does not traverse arrays, so a credential inside an array nested under auth is kept. Rule 24 (dispatch-policy.md:48) requires removal at every depth.

requirement: Empty manifests use an empty entries array and a generated marker.
Publication failure telemetry includes the manifest ID, error, and timestamp.
Driver labels are trimmed without changing their letter case.
savePlan completes validation before its first write.
Under storage-contract, announcement failure rolls back the manifest written earlier in the same operation.
finding: Same root cause as the issue 02 publishWithAnnouncement finding: handleAnnouncementFailure (manifest.mjs:32) calls store.remove on a copy returned by store.get (storage-contract.md:6), and store.remove removes nothing for any value other than the exact stored object (storage-contract.md:7). The manifest written at publisher.mjs:11 is not rolled back.

requirement: Package IDs are trimmed, deduplicated, and sorted lexically.
Package coalescing removes duplicate IDs across destination groups.
finding: Same root cause as the issue 02 coalescePackages finding: coalesceAcrossGroups (manifest.mjs:37-38) compares normalized IDs against a seen set filled with raw IDs, so a duplicate that differs only by surrounding whitespace, such as ' P1' and 'P1', is kept in a later destination group.

requirement: Under dispatch-policy, atomic plan writes remove temporary bytes when the rename operation fails.
finding: After renameTemporary rejects, the temporary bytes are locked (storage-contract.md:11). writePlanAtomically (storage.mjs:9) calls discardTemporary, which only closes the write and keeps locked bytes (storage-contract.md:13). Only removeTemporary deletes locked bytes (storage-contract.md:14), and the code does not call it. The temporary bytes therefore remain after a failed rename.

requirement: Under storage-contract, publishManifest returns, in a success result, the manifest object that store.put durably stored.
Eligible-stop execution excludes cancelled stops.
Under dispatch-policy, assigning all packages accepts a total equal to the vehicle limit.
finding: canAssignAllPackages (line 14) delegates to withinVehicleCapacity (line 3), which accepts only when remainingVehicleCapacity(...) > 0 (line 12 returns 0 at the limit). A total equal to the vehicle limit is rejected.

requirement: The public dispatch entry exports the execution operations used by callers.
finding: index.mjs re-exports no module that defines the executor operations (executor.mjs is absent from lines 1-11). Execution operations such as executeAuthorizedPlan, executeDryRun, runEligibleStops, emitPlanCreated and pendingStops are not available to callers through the public dispatch entry.

requirement: Publication success telemetry includes the manifest ID and timestamp.
Plan previews return without touching persistent storage.
Appending a stable stop returns a new list.
Dispatch backoff is capped at 2000 milliseconds.
Two plans that differ only in the order of the fields inside their nested objects have the same plan hash.
finding: withSortedKeys (line 1) wraps only the top-level plan object. JSON.stringify in serializePlan (line 3) does not apply that Proxy to nested objects, so nested key order still affects the serialized text and checksumPlan (line 7). Plans that differ only in nested key order therefore produce different hashes.

requirement: Transient retry classification requires an explicit true marker.
finding: retryTransient (retry.mjs:10) requires error.transient === true. However, publishWithRetry normalizes errors through asPublicationError (publisher.mjs:19), which marks an error transient from a finite retryAfter alone, without an explicit marker. Rule 26 (dispatch-policy.md:53) requires that treatment for requirements citing the document, while this uncited requirement requires an explicit marker. This is a governance conflict between the spec and the cited policy, reported to the Main Agent for decision.

requirement: Depot ownership requires equal actor and route depot identifiers.
Under dispatch-policy, urgent-stop partitioning places every stop in exactly one partition according to its urgency.
finding: remaining (queue.mjs:23) tests the raw stop.priority, not the effective priority from rule 15 (priorityOf, line 4). For a priority such as the string '9' or Infinity, !(stop.priority > 5) is false, and urgent (line 22) uses priorityOf, which yields 5 and is not urgent. Such a stop is in neither partition.

requirement: Destination keys are normalized with NFKC, trimmed, and uppercased.
Under dispatch-policy, the next dispatch time is the later supplied bound adjusted by Departure timing rules 10, 12, and 13.
finding: nextDispatchTime tests the blackout with candidate.getHours() (line 15), which is the local-time hour. Rule 10 (dispatch-policy.md:22) requires UTC hours, and chooseDeparture in the same module uses getUTCHours. Outside a UTC time zone the blackout check uses the wrong hour.

requirement: Plan-created telemetry is emitted only after plan storage succeeds.
finding: Same unresolved dependency as the issue 01 emitPlanCreated finding: onStored is passed as onCommit to store.write (storage.mjs:4), and docs/dispatch/storage-contract.md (lines 9-15) does not define store.write. Whether emission happens only after durable storage cannot be determined from the governing documents.

requirement: Access-log redaction removes both token and secret fields.
Under storage-contract, atomic plan writes rename the temporary bytes only after they are durable.
toStableJson uses two-space indentation and one terminal LF.
orderManifestGroups orders destination groups in ascending lexical order.
Manifest NDJSON ends every record, including the final record, with LF.
Under dispatch-policy, the ordinary stop-ordering operation follows the Stop priority rules.
finding: compareStops uses left.sequence ?? Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER (line 6) with no finite numeric check. Rule 18 (dispatch-policy.md:33) requires a stop without a finite numeric sequence to follow every equal-priority stop that has one. A string sequence such as '3' is subtracted as the number 3 and sorts before a stop with sequence 5, and a NaN sequence produces an inconsistent comparator.

requirement: Destination grouping uses normalized keys and copied records.
Batch authorization rejects the batch when any route fails depot ownership.
finding: authorizeRouteBatch returns firstRejected <= 0 (line 9). When the first route fails depot ownership, findIndex returns 0 and the function returns true, so the batch is accepted. It also returns true when no route fails, because findIndex returns -1.

requirement: Under dispatch-policy, package weighing records each package weight in the unit that the Vehicle capacity rules give.
finding: weighPackages (capacity.mjs:20) stores the value returned by scale.read without conversion. Rule 28 (dispatch-policy.md:58) requires package weights in grams, but adapter-contracts.md:8 says only that scale.read resolves to the measured weight and does not state its unit. Whether recorded weights are in grams cannot be decided from the governing documents.

requirement: Blackout intervals include the start and exclude the end.
Authorized execution rejects a caller before invoking dispatch.
finding: Same root cause as the issue 01 executeAuthorizedPlan finding: line 4 evaluates await dispatchRoute(dispatch, route) before the authorization result is applied in unlessForbidden (line 6), so dispatch is invoked for an unauthorized caller.

requirement: Successful publication results and failed publication results use distinct structured variants.
Blank package IDs make a manifest entry invalid.
Under dispatch-policy, a driver's workload counts exactly the stops whose assigned driver is that driver.
Under dispatch-policy, retry-count parsing accepts exactly the valid retry counts and rejects every other value.
finding: Same root cause as the issue 01 parseRetryCount finding: line 4 accepts Number(value) integers 0 through 3, so '' (Number('') is 0), ' 2 ', '0x2', '1e0', null and false are accepted, while rule 22 (dispatch-policy.md:43) accepts only one or more base-10 digits.

requirement: Serialized plan parsing returns structured success or failure.
Under dispatch-policy, the delivered-stop count counts exactly the delivered stops.
The ordinary stop-ordering operation sorts a copy of its input.
Stops at the vehicle weight limit remain in the accepted partition.
Given a positive integer maximum, manifest chunks never exceed that configured size.
normalizeRouteKey applies NFKC before trimming and uppercasing.
Normalized plan storage keys trim and uppercase route keys.
Under dispatch-policy, measured vehicle limits use the unit that the Vehicle capacity rules give.
Under dispatch-policy, publication retries stop immediately for failures that the Failure classification rules do not make transient.
finding: Same root cause as the issue 02 publishWithRetry finding: asPublicationError (publisher.mjs:19) marks a failure marked transient: false as transient when retryAfter is finite. Rule 27 (dispatch-policy.md:54) makes it never transient, so publication does not stop immediately and retries it.

requirement: UTF-8 encoding uses the explicit utf8 encoding name.
Under dispatch-policy, a suspended actor cannot plan any route.
finding: Same root cause as the issue 01 canPlanRoute suspended-actor finding: effectiveScopes (line 5) keeps active claim scopes for a suspended actor, so a suspended actor with an active routes:plan claim can plan a route on a matching depot. Rule 5 (dispatch-policy.md:11) says a suspended actor has no held scopes.

requirement: Under dispatch-policy, delivery notices go to the contact phone of every manifest entry.
finding: sendDeliveryNotices passes entry.phone unchanged to sms.send (publisher.mjs:31). Rule 33 (dispatch-policy.md:66) defines the contact phone as the phone with every space and hyphen removed, and manifestRecipients (manifest.mjs:44) applies that normalization, but the delivery path does not.

requirement: Under dispatch-policy, the next retry delay follows the Retry timing rules whenever the server provides retryAfter.
finding: Same root cause as the issue 01 nextRetryDelay finding: nextRetryDelay (retry.mjs:24) takes the retry-after path only for truthy retryAfter, so a server-provided retryAfter of 0 falls through to computeBackoff instead of replacing it under rule 7 (dispatch-policy.md:16).
